doc.title: Jackie Cain and Roy Kral interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

title: 'A Wilder Alias' and the aftermath of their loss
summary: The angrier album recorded after their daughter's and drummer Jimmy Molinari's deaths, and Niki's Song.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Well you certainly have not been afraid to take some chances. Now I want to get the chronology right. The time you did “Time and Love.” And then I remember liking that album and going out and getting another one, I’m not sure whether it came before it or —
Probably after.
And it had big stones on it? Like a desert kind of scene or something.
“A Wilder Alias.”
That’s the one. Now that was much different.
It was so different.
It was much more adventurous.
There was rage in it.

Well not all of it but some of it. That’s right after our daughter died. And also the drummer that worked with us, Jimmy Molinari, he’d been with us a while, he got killed. Somebody killed him down in Manhattan somewhere. And we don’t know the —
It was two weeks after our daughter died, and Jimmy—
It was a double whammy you know.
It was something, I don’t know what he got into, but he was just killed and thrown off a roof.
We really don’t know what happened. Nobody knows.
So this album came out and it was that first tune—
“A Wilder Alias.”
“A Wilder Alias.” Because I said what Jimmy needed was A Wilder Alias to get away from whatever he was doing. Now a lot of people thought this was A. Wilder.
Alec Wilder. And people who bought it thought that. Some of them.
And here is some of this crazy music.

It was kind of fierce music in there, you know, some of it, well one of them was, that particular song, “A Wilder Alias,” and it had a lot of anger in it and stuff I think. But then there was other things that were softer. “Niki’s Song” was her favorite song and we did that, the one about the beach, it originally was called “A Full Moon” and then we changed it to “Niki’s Song.” Creed said we should do it. I said that was Niki’s favorite song, he said well why don’t you call it that. So that was on and that was pleasant. But I think a lot of people were disappointed in it, I mean just the average person. A lot of musicians liked it. But then there were a lot of people that didn’t like it because it wasn’t typical Jackie and Roy, smiley, happy-go-lucky, clever.
Yeah well that’s not where you life was at right then, was it?
That’s right. Your music reflects your life you know. So I don’t think that CD or album did very well.
But Creed gave us full freedom, as always, just do it.
